findings.evidence: There are no definite opacities visible in the right mid lung on the provided frontal and lateral chest radiographs. The lung fields appear clear.

verdict.limitations: The assessment of cardiac size is limited by the single frontal and lateral views provided. A more accurate assessment would require additional views or modalities, and patient-specific factors such as body habitus and inspiration level can influence the apparent cardiac size on plain radiographs. The lateral view is not ideal for assessing cardiac size due to magnification and superimposition of structures. The provided images are two-dimensional radiographs, which may obscure subtle opacities due to superimposition of structures. Without prior imaging for comparison, it is difficult to assess for interval changes. The quality of the images is adequate for general assessment, but very small or subtle findings might be missed.
